cast.name: Dr. Richard ("Doc B")
cast.catchphrase: Nature already wrote the playbook—our job is to learn how to read it in zero-G!
cast.bio_k5: The friendly space plant scientist who helps seedlings, mushrooms, and astronauts thrive on the Moon and Mars!
cast.bio_ms: Director of the Collaborative Science Environment (CoSE) and Chair of the NASA GeneLab Plant Analysis Working Group.
cast.bio_hs: Principal Investigator integrating spaceflight multi-omics, computational fluid dynamics (CFD), mycoponics, and serious games for bioregenerative life support.

cast.name: Sprout
cast.catchphrase: No gravity? Stagnant air? Cosmic rays? Watch my genes adapt!
cast.bio_k5: A brave little green sprout who flew to the International Space Station to show us how plants grow among the stars.
cast.bio_ms: The world's favorite model plant! Because its entire genome is mapped, Sprout reveals how roots, leaves, and cells sense space.
cast.bio_hs: Arabidopsis thaliana ecotype Col-0/WS—the flagship model organism across NASA OSDR transcriptomic, proteomic, and epigenomic flight studies.

cast.name: Myco
cast.catchphrase: Give me lunar dust and crop scraps, and I'll build you a living habitat!
cast.bio_k5: A glowing underground web of friendly fungal threads that recycles waste and glues Moon dust into strong bricks.
cast.bio_ms: Fungal mycelium connects ecosystems, unlocks minerals from crushed rock, and manufactures medicines and food in closed habitats.
cast.bio_hs: Filamentous fungi engineered for solid-state fermentation, mycoponic nutrient mobilization, regolith biocomposites, and biosynthetic gene cluster (BGC) discovery.

cast.name: Statolith
cast.catchphrase: On Earth I sink to point 'DOWN'—in orbit I float and party!
cast.bio_k5: A tiny heavy starch pebble inside root tip cells that rolls downhill so roots know which way to dig.
cast.bio_ms: Dense starch-filled plastids inside columella cells that sediment under gravity to trigger auxin hormone redistribution.
cast.bio_hs: Columella amyloplasts governed by Stokes sedimentation, Brownian motion, and actin-cytoskeletal mechanics across fractional gravity (0g, 0.166g, 0.38g, 1g).

cast.name: Pixel
cast.catchphrase: Beep-boop! Turning 10 billion data points into one clear picture!
cast.bio_k5: A super-smart hologram helper who reads plant DNA messages and draws 3D maps of invisible air currents.
cast.bio_ms: An AI engine that combines computer vision, fluid physics simulators, and NASA gene databases right in your web browser.
cast.bio_hs: Embodies CoSE's open-source machine learning stack: CVAE autoencoders, Lattice-Boltzmann CFD, TabPFN, Cellpose segmentation, and NASA-IBM foundation models.

cast.name: Commander Astra
cast.catchphrase: Healthy plants keep astronauts strong—and healthy astronauts keep the mission alive!
cast.bio_k5: An astronaut gardener growing fresh space tomatoes and testing how to keep muscles and bones strong in zero gravity.
cast.bio_ms: Monitors crew biomarkers, harvests VEGGIE salad crops, and tests how space food protects the human body on long voyages.
cast.bio_hs: Translates cross-species OSDR & JAXA cell-free RNA signatures, LINCS L1000 drug-gene reversals, and mineral bioavailability into crew health countermeasures.

series.title: Invisible Winds: Gas Transport & Spaceflight Biophysics
series.description: When gravity vanishes, buoyant air convection stops! Discover how invisible stagnant air blankets wrap around space leaves—and how computational fluid dynamics (CFD) helps plants breathe on the Moon and ISS.

series.title: Code of the Cosmos: Spaceflight Multi-Omics & Epigenetic Decoders
series.description: Every cell in space is writing an emergency logbook in RNA, proteins, and chromatin! Follow Pixel and Sprout as AI autoencoders decode circadian clocks, alternative splicing, and single-cell spaceflight atlases.

series.title: Shields of the Solar System: Radiation, Magnetobiology & Quantum Spin
series.art_style_name: Silver-Age Cosmic Sci-Fi & Jack Kirby Energy
series.description: Beyond Earth's magnetic umbrella, galactic cosmic rays and near-null magnetic fields challenge living cells. Explore quantum radical pairs, planetary magnetic anomalies, and DNA repair superpowers!

series.title: Roots in Orbit: Seeds, Signaling Waves & Space Crop Physiology
series.description: From the first drop of water waking a dormant seed to calcium lightning waves, auxin fountains, and dwarf space tomatoes—witness the living poetry of plants adapting to orbit.

series.title: From Dust to Life: Regolith, Mycoponics & Closed-Loop Ecosystems
series.description: How do you turn sharp, lifeless lunar dust into a thriving green farm? Join Myco and Doc B as fungi, sintered ceramics, and 180 years of Earth agronomy close the loop for lunar habitats.

series.title: Crew Vital: Astronaut Health, Biomarkers & Space Nutrition
series.description: Microgravity weakens muscles and leaches bone minerals—unless space biology fights back! See how multi-omics and fresh space-grown crops protect Commander Astra on the road to Mars.

series.title: Science for Everyone: Open Phenomics, AI Vision & Classroom Tools
series.description: No supercomputer? No problem! Discover how browser-based ImageJ, root-tracing AI, color calibration cards, and 3D anatomical atlases put NASA-grade instruments into every K–12 classroom.

series.title: Play to Discover: Serious Simulations, Space Arcade & Citizen Science
series.description: Before we build a city on the Moon, we simulate it! Step inside the CoSE Space Arcade and Academy where every game tests real engineering bottlenecks, resource loops, and student hypotheses.

concepts.name: Microgravity & Buoyancy Loss
concepts.k5: In space, everything floats together—so warm air doesn't rise and heavy things don't sink!
concepts.ms: Without gravity-driven buoyancy, natural convection stops and fluids move mainly by slow diffusion or fans.
concepts.hs: As gravitational acceleration g approaches 0, the Grashof and Rayleigh numbers collapse, eliminating buoyant natural convection.

concepts.name: Boundary-Layer Physics & CFD
concepts.k5: An invisible pillow of still air wraps around leaves in space, making it harder to breathe CO2 and O2.
concepts.ms: Stagnant air boundary layers thicken around leaves in low gravity, slowing down gas exchange and water evaporation.
concepts.hs: Computational Fluid Dynamics (Lattice-Boltzmann & OpenFOAM) quantifies diffusive boundary-layer resistance (rb) scaling as g decreases.

concepts.name: Photorespiration & Carbon Balance
concepts.k5: When a leaf traps its own oxygen bubble, its solar sugar factory accidentally runs in reverse!
concepts.ms: Trapped oxygen inside space leaves causes Rubisco to grab O2 instead of CO2, wasting energy in photorespiration.
concepts.hs: Coupled FvCB photosynthesis-conductance modeling reveals O2/CO2 boundary-layer trapping drives spaceflight photorespiratory gene induction.

concepts.name: Gravitropism & Auxin Steering
concepts.k5: Tiny starch pebbles inside root tips roll downhill to tell roots which way is down!
concepts.ms: Statolith sedimentation redirects the growth hormone auxin so roots curve toward gravity and shoots grow toward light.
concepts.hs: Amyloplast sedimentation kinetics and PIN-mediated polar auxin transport govern root gravitropic curvature across altered gravity vectors.

concepts.name: Cosmic Radiation & DNA Repair
concepts.k5: High-speed space particles zoom through space like tiny darts, so cells use protective shields and DNA repair crews!
concepts.ms: Galactic cosmic rays and solar protons damage DNA and create reactive molecules, triggering emergency repair genes.
concepts.hs: High-LET ionizing radiation (GCR/SPE) induces double-strand breaks, activating SOG1-dependent DNA damage response and antioxidant networks.

concepts.name: Magnetobiology & Quantum Spin
concepts.k5: Earth has a giant magnetic shield, and living cells have tiny quantum compasses that notice when it's gone!
concepts.ms: The Moon and Mars lack Earth's global magnetic field; plants sense near-null magnetic fields through light-sensitive proteins.
concepts.hs: Flavin-tryptophan radical-pair spin dynamics in cryptochromes and Fe-S clusters couple weak magnetic fields to redox signaling.

concepts.name: Spaceflight Multi-Omics (NASA OSDR)
concepts.k5: By reading thousands of plant and astronaut gene messages stored in NASA's library, we can spot space stress patterns!
concepts.ms: Transcriptomics, proteomics, and metabolomics measure which genes and molecules turn on or off during spaceflight.
concepts.hs: Meta-analysis across NASA Open Science Data Repository (OSDR) harmonizes bulk/single-cell RNA-seq, proteome, and metabolome contrasts.

concepts.name: 3D & Single-Cell Digital Twins
concepts.k5: Not every cell in a plant does the same job—3D digital twins let us zoom inside each organ and cell type!
concepts.ms: Interactive 3D models combine anatomy with cell-specific gene data so we can see how roots, leaves, and seeds respond.
concepts.hs: Single-nucleus deconvolution and 3D biophysical digital twins resolve cell-type-specific trajectories from bulk spaceflight omics.

concepts.name: Epigenetics, Chromatin & Splicing
concepts.k5: Cells can fold up their DNA recipe book or remix chapters to make new tools for space survival!
concepts.ms: Chemical tags on DNA packaging (chromatin) and alternative RNA splicing change how genes are read without mutating DNA.
concepts.hs: Polycomb H3K27me3 chromatin states and coordinate spliceosome remodeling govern transcriptional repression and plasticity in orbit.

concepts.name: Clocks, Calcium Waves & ROS Signals
concepts.k5: Plants have internal 24-hour clocks and send glowing calcium and oxygen Morse-code flashes from root to leaf!
concepts.ms: With 16 sunrises a day on the ISS, plants rely on circadian rhythms, calcium waves, and reactive oxygen species (ROS) to stay coordinated.
concepts.hs: ChronoGauge phase decoding, CVAE redox kinetics, and GCaMP fluorescence quantification resolve systemic stress signaling dynamics.

concepts.name: Mycoponics & Fungal Biomanufacturing
concepts.k5: Friendly mushrooms team up with plant roots to share food, recycle leftovers, and make space medicines!
concepts.ms: Fungal mycelium digests tough plant waste, unlocks trapped minerals, and synthesizes useful compounds in space habitats.
concepts.hs: Mycoponic co-cultivation and curated MIBiG biosynthetic gene clusters (BGCs) enable solid-state biomanufacturing and nutrient cycling.

concepts.name: Lunar & Martian Regolith (ISRU)
concepts.k5: We can't pack heavy dirt on a rocket—so we learn to bake Moon dust into plant pots and turn crushed rock into soil!
concepts.ms: In-Situ Resource Utilization (ISRU) uses local lunar and Martian regolith for radiation shielding, ceramics, and crop growth.
concepts.hs: Sintered regolith ceramics, ARES astromaterial curation, and growth-anchored regolith meta-analysis guide extraterrestrial substrate design.

concepts.name: Closed-Loop Life Support (BLSS)
concepts.k5: People breathe out CO2 that plants love, and plants make the oxygen and food that people need—one big space family circle!
concepts.ms: Bioregenerative Life Support Systems recycle carbon, water, and nutrients between astronauts, crops, and microbes.
concepts.hs: Stoichiometric carbon/water/energy balance modeling and historical agro-ecosystem datasets (Rothamsted/EDEN ISS) quantify BLSS resilience.

concepts.name: Astronaut Health & Countermeasures
concepts.k5: Floating in space makes muscles and bones lazy, so astronauts eat super-nutritious space veggies and exercise every day!
concepts.ms: Spaceflight alters muscle genes, calcium/mineral balance, and blood biomarkers; targeted nutrition helps keep crews healthy.
concepts.hs: Cross-species muscle atrophy meta-analysis, LINCS L1000 transcriptomic reversal, and LSDA mineral analytics identify dietary countermeasures.

concepts.name: Computer Vision & Open Phenomics
concepts.k5: Smart cameras and color-check cards let students measure roots, seeds, and leaf colors right in a web browser!
concepts.ms: Calibrated imaging and machine learning turn smartphone or microscope photos into precise scientific measurements.
concepts.hs: ArUco/Munsell color calibration, photon-transfer noise modeling, Cellpose/RootPainter segmentation, and browser WebAssembly ImageJ democratize phenomics.

concepts.name: Serious Simulations & Citizen Science
concepts.k5: Playing space colony games lets you test your own Moon farm ideas and learn how real mission engineers solve puzzles!
concepts.ms: Interactive simulations and classroom citizen-science kits let students form hypotheses, run experiments, and analyze real data.
concepts.hs: Pre/post-hypothesis serious games, LLM game-theory environments, and FAIR Jupyter curricula evaluate systems thinking in space architecture.
